steps.title: Sterilize bench and rinse sample
steps.instruction: Clean all bench surfaces with 70 % ethanol and/or Lysol. Remove reef seawater from the sampling container, wipe the exterior and the surrounding drain/waste area, then refill the container with sterile seawater filtered through a 0.2 µm cellulose‑nitrate membrane and autoclaved; wipe the exterior again. Vigorously shake or swirl the container for 30 s to loosen particulates, let stand for 2 min, swirl again, and decant the particulate‑laden seawater into a waste beaker. Repeat the refill‑shake‑rest‑swirl‑decant cycle two more times (three rinses total). After the final rinse, transfer the invertebrate to a sterile glass beaker containing sterile seawater. Optional: let the organism sit 5–10 min to allow flushing of particles.

substeps.instruction: Clean bench with 70 % ethanol and/or Lysol.
Remove seawater from sampling container and wipe exterior and drain area.
Refill container with sterile seawater (0.2 µm filtered, autoclaved) and wipe exterior again.
Shake/swirl for 30 s, rest 2 min, swirl again, decant waste seawater.
Repeat refill‑shake‑rest‑swirl‑decant two more times.
Transfer invertebrate to sterile glass beaker with sterile seawater.
Optional: let sit 5–10 min for flushing.

steps.title: Excise tissue and add glass beads
steps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel or razor blade, remove 0.2–0.3 mL of tissue from each invertebrate (perform in triplicate) and place each aliquot into a sterile 2 mL microcentrifuge tube. For very thin tissue over a calcium carbonate skeleton, the whole sample may be homogenized with a mortar and pestle instead. Add 0.5 mL of a sterilized glass‑bead mixture (e.g., 0.1 g 0.5 mm beads, 0.15 g 0.1 mm beads, 0.4 g 1.0 mm beads, and three 1.3 mm beads) to each tube. Fill each tube with sterile seawater up to the 2 mL mark and seal the tube tops with parafilm.

substeps.instruction: Remove 0.2–0.3 mL tissue with sterile scalpel/razor blade; place in sterile 2 mL tube (triplicate).
If tissue is very thin over calcium carbonate, process whole sample with mortar and pestle.
Add 0.5 mL sterilized glass‑bead mixture (specified composition) to each tube.
Fill to 2 mL with sterile seawater.
Seal tube tops with parafilm.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue‑bead mixture
steps.instruction: Homogenize each sealed tube using a vortex mixer or a FastPrep instrument. Perform disruption cycles, returning tubes to ice between cycles to keep the sample cold.

steps.title: Centrifuge to remove debris
steps.instruction: First spin the homogenized tubes at 3,200 × g for 16 min at 4 °C. Transfer as much supernatant as possible to a new sterile 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube; if the volume is low, add sterile seawater to bring the volume to approximately 1.2 mL. Centrifuge this supernatant at 16,000 × g for 17 min at 4 °C. Transfer the resulting supernatant to another sterile 1.5 mL tube and dilute to the 1.0 mL mark with sterile seawater.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3,200 × g for 16 min, 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to new 1.5 mL tube; dilute to ~1.2 mL if needed.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 17 min, 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to new 1.5 mL tube and dilute to 1.0 mL with sterile seawater.

steps.title: Precipitate viruses with PEG
steps.instruction: Add 250–300 µL of 5× polyethylene glycol (PEG) solution (BioVision catalog #K904) to the supernatant in the 1.5 mL tube. Mix gently and incubate the tube overnight (≥12 h) at 4 °C. After incubation, centrifuge at 3,200 × g for 30 min at 4 °C. Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet (pipette or decant). Resuspend the pellet in ~1 mL sterile seawater, or, for a higher concentration, in ~200 µL virus‑resuspension liquid (BioVision catalog #K904). Dilute further if a larger volume is required for downstream isolation.

substeps.instruction: Add 250–300 µL 5× PEG (BioVision #K904) to supernatant.
Incubate ≥12 h at 4 °C.
Centrifuge at 3,200 × g for 30 min, 4 °C.
Remove supernatant carefully without disturbing pellet.
Resuspend pellet in ~1 mL sterile seawater or ~200 µL virus‑resuspension liquid (BioVision #K904).
Dilute further if needed for downstream work.
